title: Iranian Drones Strike Near US Consulate in Erbil as Conflict Enters Fragile Ceasefire
excerpt: Multiple explosions rocked Iraq's Kurdish capital last week as Iran and the US exchange fire across the Middle East, with Trump now claiming 'good talks' with Tehran.
body:
• Iranian drones targeted the US consulate area in Erbil, Iraq's Kurdish capital, with Kurdish counter-terrorism forces intercepting five to six explosive-laden drones on July 24
  • A US soldier was killed during a controlled detonation of a downed Iranian drone at Erbil Air Base, bringing total American military deaths in the conflict to at least 18
  • Washington suspended its two-week bombing campaign against Iran on Saturday, with Trump claiming the sides are having "good talks" through mediators
  • Iran claims it destroyed "almost all" US military infrastructure in Erbil, though these assertions have not been independently verified

Multiple explosions shook Erbil, the capital of Iraq's semi-autonomous Kurdish region, as Iranian drones targeted areas near the US consulate and a military base at the city's international airport. The attacks came during one of the most volatile stretches of the five-month-old US-Iran conflict, which has now entered an uncertain ceasefire.

Kurdistan Counter-Terrorism Service forces intercepted between five and six explosive-laden one-way attack drones over Erbil on July 24, according to Iraqi media. An Associated Press journalist on the ground heard at least seven blasts and witnessed four plumes of black smoke rising from areas near the airport base hosting US forces.

American Casualties Mount

The attacks have exacted a human toll. Sergeant Michael Emmanuel Swinton, 30, of Fayetteville, North Carolina, was killed during a controlled detonation of a downed Iranian drone at Erbil Air Base. Three other US service members — 1st Lt. Tyler James Feehan, 25; Pvt. Isabella Gonzales, 19; and Sgt. Angel Rampersad, 28 — were killed in an Iranian strike on Muwaffaq Salti Air Base in Jordan on July 17.

The Pentagon's official casualty database lists 14 deaths and 420 injuries over the course of the conflict, though the actual toll appears higher. The database briefly showed 18 deaths before reverting, with the discrepancy attributed to what a Pentagon spokesman called "temporary data disruptions."

From Bombing to Ceasefire

Washington abruptly suspended its two-week campaign of air strikes against Iran on Saturday, following advice from military commanders who said the bombing had reached the limits of what it could achieve. The chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, General Dan Caine, had expressed concern over the depletion of air munitions.

President Trump struck an optimistic tone on Monday, telling reporters aboard Air Force One: "We're having good talks. I think there's a good chance that something could happen, and if it doesn't, we go back to doing what we were doing two days ago."

"This is not in our DNA."

— Esmail Baghaei, Iran's Foreign Ministry Spokesman, rejecting reports that Tehran had requested negotiations

Tehran has pushed back against the characterisation that it sought talks. Iran's Foreign Ministry said messages were being passed through mediators, but spokesman Esmail Baghaei called reports of Iran requesting negotiations "fabricated." A senior Iranian official told Reuters that Iran would halt its own attacks as long as Trump's self-imposed ceasefire continued.

Regional Spillover

The conflict has expanded well beyond Iraq. Iran's army spokesman, Brigadier General Mohammad Reza Akraminia, claimed that Iranian forces had destroyed "almost all" US military infrastructure in Erbil during the 40-day conflict — claims Reuters could not independently verify. Iran also struck targets in Kuwait, Bahrain, and Jordan, while its Houthi allies in Yemen targeted Saudi Arabia's East-West oil pipeline.

Oil prices, which had briefly topped $100 per barrel last week, tumbled around 8.2 percent on Monday as the ceasefire took hold, with Brent crude falling to just below $89.

What It Means for India

The escalation directly affects India's strategic and economic interests. Iraq remains a major crude oil supplier to India, and any sustained disruption to Erbil's airport — a logistics hub for international oil companies operating in the Kurdistan Region — could ripple through supply chains. The Strait of Hormuz, through which roughly one-fifth of the world's oil transits, has become a flashpoint, with Iran asserting control over shipping lanes and Trump demanding free passage.

For the estimated 8 million Indians living across the Gulf states, the expanding geography of the conflict — stretching from Iran to Jordan, Kuwait, Bahrain, and Saudi Arabia — raises safety concerns. The Indian embassy in Baghdad has urged citizens to exercise caution.

What's Next

The ceasefire's durability remains uncertain. Washington and Tehran reached a framework agreement in June for talks by the end of August on major issues including Iran's nuclear program and Strait of Hormuz access. But the two sides dispute the meaning of the memorandum's language, with Washington insisting it requires free transit while Iran claims authority to supervise passage. Drone attacks by Iran-backed groups on Saudi Arabia, Jordan, and Iraq on Monday — just hours after Trump's optimistic remarks — suggest that even if the principals are talking, their proxies are not standing down.
